questions.q: What does the psalmist say about what Yahweh has done?
questions.a: The psalmist says that people should tell everyone about what Yahweh has done.

questions.q: Who does the psalmist tell to rejoice?
questions.a: The psalmist tells those who seek Yahweh to rejoice.

questions.q: How often should people seek the presence of Yahweh?
questions.a: The psalmist calls people to seek his presence continually.

questions.q: For how long does the psalmist say Yahweh remembers his covenant?
questions.a: The psalmist says Yahweh remembers his covenant forever.

questions.q: What covenant does the psalmist say Yahweh calls to mind?
questions.a: Yahweh calls to mind the covenant that he made with Abraham and his oath to Isaac.

questions.q: What has Yahweh given as an inheritance to Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh promised Israel that the land of Canaan will be what they and their descendants inherit from him.

questions.q: When did Yahweh make the covenant with Israel?
questions.a: The psalmist says that Yahweh made this covenant with Israel when they were only few in number and strangers in that land.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh tell kings not to touch?
questions.a: Yahweh told them not to harm his chosen people or his prophets.

questions.q: How did Yahweh send Joseph ahead of Israel?
questions.a: He sent Joseph ahead of them by having him sold by his brothers as a slave.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for Joseph while he was in prison?
questions.a: While he was in prison, Yahweh taught Joseph to trust him more.

questions.q: What role did the king give Joseph?
questions.a: The king appointed Joseph as lord of his house and ruler over all of his possessions.

questions.q: Where did Jacob live when he came to Egypt?
questions.a: Jacob lived for a time in the land of Ham.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh cause to hate his people?
questions.a: Yahweh caused the rulers of Egypt to hate the people of Israel.

questions.q: Where did Moses and Aaron perform Yahweh’s signs?
questions.a: Moses and Aaron performed Yahweh’s signs among the Egyptians who lived in the land of Ham.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do to the Egyptians’ water and fish?
questions.a: Yahweh turned the Egyptians’ water into blood and killed their fish.

questions.q: What did Yahweh send along with the hail in Egypt?
questions.a: Along with the hail, Yahweh sent fire that burned throughout their land.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh kill in Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh killed every firstborn son of the Egyptians.

questions.q: Why were the people of Egypt glad when the Israelites went away?
questions.a: The Egyptians were glad when the Israelites went away because they had become very afraid of the Israelites.

questions.q: With what kind of food did Yahweh provide for the Israelites?
questions.a: Yahweh satisfied them with quail to eat and bread from heaven.

questions.q: Which holy promise did Yahweh remember?
questions.a: Yahweh remembered his holy promise that he made to Abraham his servant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh give his people?
questions.a: He gave his people the land and planted fields of the people that lived there.

commentary.text: A solemn call to praise and serve the Lord.
Their deliverance from Egypt, and their settlement in Canaan.

Verses 1–7 Our devotion is here stirred up, that we may stir up ourselves to praise God. Seek his strength; that is, his grace; the strength of his Spirit to work in us that which is good, which we cannot do but by strength derived from him, for which he will be sought. Seek to have his favour to eternity, therefore continue seeking it while living in this world; for he will not only be found, but he will reward those that diligently seek him.

Let us remember the Redeemer's marvellous works, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth. Though true Christians are few number, strangers and pilgrims upon earth, yet a far better inheritance than Canaan is made sure to them by the covenant of God; and if we have the anointing of the Holy Spirit, none can do us any harm. Afflictions are among our mercies. They prove our faith and love, they humble our pride, they wean us from the world, and quicken our prayers. Bread is the staff which supports life; when that staff is broken, the body fails and sinks to the earth. The word of God is the staff of spiritual life, the food and support of the soul: the sorest judgment is a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. Such a famine was sore in all lands when Christ appeared in the flesh; whose coming, and the blessed effect of it, are shadowed forth in the history of Joseph. At the appointed time Christ was exalted as Mediator; all the treasures of grace and salvation are at his disposal, perishing sinners come to him, and are relieved by him.

As the believer commonly thrives best in his soul when under the cross; so the church also flourishes most in true holiness, and increases in number, while under persecution. Yet instruments shall be raised up for their deliverance, and plagues may be expected by persecutors. And see the special care God took of his people in the wilderness. All the benefits bestowed on Israel as a nation, were shadows of spiritual blessings with which we are blessed in Christ Jesus. Having redeemed us with his blood, restored our souls to holiness, and set us at liberty from Satan's bondage, he guides and guards us all the way. He satisfies our souls with the bread of heaven, and the water of life from the Rock of salvation, and will bring us safely to heaven. He redeems his servants from all iniquity, and purifies them unto himself, to be a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
